To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
academic research on capital gains taxation has been effective, but only to a limited extent, in changing policy.

(a) academic economists have not developed a theory of the role of their research in the political process, (b) academic economists have been unable to persuade influential consumers of their ideas to change the way they make policy decisions, and (c) the debate over the taxation of capital gains illustrates that the rhetoric of academic economics is not effective in influencing policy makers.

the academic literature on capital gains taxation is inconclusive; that policymakers do not use the academic literature to inform policy decisions; that the academic rhetoric is ineffective in influencing policymakers; and that a process analysis of the policy process is a superior way to understand the gap between academic research and policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of economics in the policy-making process.
how economic knowledge is created and used in the political sphere.
the role of academic knowledge in the policy-making process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rhetoric of the academic community is ineffective in the policy arena.
academic economists have been largely unsuccessful in influencing policy on the taxation of capital gains in the United States.
the academic debate on capital gains taxation has not been influential on the policy debate, but it has had a positive influence on the quality of the public debate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
academic economists have not been very successful in influencing policy makers on the question of capital gains taxation.
, in the absence of an explicit model of how ideas influence political decision making, academic rhetoric has little effect on political decision making.
academic rhetoric has a limited impact on policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gap is not due to a lack of influence of academic ideas.
, although the rhetoric of academic economists is sometimes at variance with the policy rhetoric, the two are often complementary and mutually reinforcing.
, in order to be more effective, academic economists must develop a theory of the policy process that incorporates the rhetorical gap.
